Definition: , or simpler στρωννύω; prolongation from a still simpler στρόω, (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to G4731 through the idea of positing); to "strew," i.e. spread (as a carpet or couch):--make bed, furnish, spread, strew.
BiblicalUsage: To spread is to make ready, and the word covers a bed, a room, and a road. Arise, and make thy bed, Peter tells Aeneas; the upper room is furnished, make ready there; and the multitude spread their garments in the way and strawed branches before the King.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the spreading is preparation in three kinds: a bed for the healed, a room for the supper, and a road for the King.
